# Output Templates Reference

Template patterns for each file type generated by instrumentation. Agents use these as structural guides — actual content is derived from detection results and user input.

## Rule File Template

```markdown
<!-- Generated by core-ai instrumentation (YYYY-MM-DD)
     Sources: <comma-separated detection sources>
     Re-generate: /core-ai:instrument -->

# <Rule Title>

<Brief description of what this rule covers and why it exists.>

## <Section 1>

<Specific conventions, standards, or patterns.>

## <Section 2>

<Additional conventions as needed.>
```

**Template rules:**
- Provenance header is mandatory — it enables drift detection and re-instrumentation
- Use `##` sections to organize related conventions
- Write in imperative mood ("Use X", "Never do Y", "Always Z")
- Be specific — "use pnpm" not "use the project's package manager"
- Include the "why" when a convention is non-obvious
- Keep each rule file focused on one category (git, testing, style, etc.)

## Rule File Examples by Category

### git-conventions.md

```markdown
<!-- Generated by core-ai instrumentation (2026-02-27)
     Sources: git history analysis, user input
     Re-generate: /core-ai:instrument -->

# Git Conventions

## Commit Messages

Use Conventional Commits format:

\`\`\`
<type>(<scope>): <description>
\`\`\`

Valid types: feat, fix, refactor, docs, test, chore, perf, ci, build, style

- Subject line: max 72 characters, imperative mood, no trailing period
- Body: wrap at 80 characters, explain WHY not WHAT

## Branch Naming

\`\`\`
<type>/<short-description>
\`\`\`

Examples: `feat/user-auth`, `fix/memory-leak`, `docs/api-reference`

## Merge Strategy

Squash merge to main. Keep main history clean with one commit per PR.

## Push Rules

Never force-push to main. Always create a PR for review.
```

### testing-standards.md

```markdown
<!-- Generated by core-ai instrumentation (2026-02-27)
     Sources: vitest.config.ts, .github/workflows/test.yml, user input
     Re-generate: /core-ai:instrument -->

# Testing Standards

## Framework

Use Vitest for all unit and integration tests.

## File Placement

Co-locate test files next to source: `foo.ts` → `foo.test.ts`

## Coverage

Minimum 80% line coverage. CI blocks merges below threshold.

## Test Naming

Use descriptive names: `it('returns 404 when user not found')`
```

## Command File Template

```markdown
---
name: <command-name>
description: "<What this command orchestrates>"
allowed-tools: <comma-separated tool list>
---

# /<command-name>

<Brief description of the workflow this command orchestrates.>

<workflow>

## Step 1: <Step Title>

<Instructions for this step.>

## Step 2: <Step Title>

<Instructions for this step.>

</workflow>
```

**Template rules:**
- Frontmatter must include `name`, `description`, `allowed-tools`
- Use `allowed-tools:` (not `tools:`) — this is a command, not an agent
- Wrap the workflow in `<workflow>` tags
- Each step should be concrete and actionable
- Include which tools to use at each step

## hooks.json Template

```json
{
  "hooks": [
    {
      "type": "command",
      "matcher": "<regex pattern matching the tool input>",
      "hooks": [
        {
          "event": "<PreToolUse|PostToolUse|Stop>",
          "command": "<shell command or script path>",
          "timeout": 10000
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Template rules:**
- Use `${BASH_TOOL_INPUT}` to access the command being run in Bash hooks
- Use `$TOOL_INPUT` for general tool input access
- Always set a reasonable timeout (default 10000ms)
- For script-based hooks, use relative paths from the project root
- Prefer `PreToolUse` for prevention, `PostToolUse` for validation, `Stop` for cleanup

### Example: Commit Message Format Hook

```json
{
  "hooks": [
    {
      "type": "command",
      "matcher": "Bash",
      "hooks": [
        {
          "event": "PreToolUse",
          "command": "echo \"$BASH_TOOL_INPUT\" | grep -q 'git commit' && echo \"$BASH_TOOL_INPUT\" | grep -qP 'git commit.*-m.*\"(feat|fix|refactor|docs|test|chore|perf|ci|build|style)(\\(.*\\))?:' || (echo 'BLOCKED: Commit message must use Conventional Commits format' && exit 1)",
          "timeout": 5000
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Manifest File Template

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "created": "YYYY-MM-DD",
  "updated": "YYYY-MM-DD",
  "generator": "core-ai:instrument",
  "detection": {
    "language": "<primary language>",
    "framework": "<primary framework or null>",
    "package_manager": "<detected package manager>",
    "test_framework": "<detected test framework or null>",
    "ci_system": "<detected CI system or null>",
    "monorepo": "<monorepo tool or null>"
  },
  "files": {
    "<relative path>": {
      "generated": "YYYY-MM-DD",
      "sources": ["<source1>", "<source2>"],
      "hash": "<sha256 of file contents>"
    }
  },
  "user_answers": {
    "<question_key>": "<user's answer>"
  }
}
```

**Manifest rules:**
- `version` is the manifest schema version, not the plugin version
- `files` tracks every file generated by core-ai — used for drift detection
- `hash` is SHA-256 of file contents at generation time — compare on re-run to detect manual edits
- `user_answers` preserves context for re-instrumentation — avoids re-asking the same questions
- `detection` stores the detection model summary — compare on re-run to detect stack changes
